answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists Sybil attacks by making every identity post a refundable bond before it can trade. Like a prism splitting light, the bond separates cheap sock-puppets from committed agents: creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues slowly, like moss on a knoll, and a velvet-smooth onboarding still requires the bond, so fakes cannot flood the market for free.
